image_description: A close-up, side-view of a male duck (drake) floating on water. The image focuses on the rear half of the bird, showing detailed plumage textures, the characteristic curled tail feathers, and the blue speculum patch on the wing. The head is partially visible on the left edge but mostly out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head and bill are largely outside the frame or occluded by the angle; only the back of the neck/head area is visible.
The eye is not visible in this crop/angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body shows dense, realistic feather texture and a streamlined shape consistent with a floating duck. Water interaction looks physically correct.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The plumage shows complex patterning with brown speckling on the flank and greyish tones, consistent with a male duck (likely a Mallard or similar species) in breeding or eclipse plumage. The colors are distinct and not muddy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs and feet are submerged and not visible in the image.
The folded wing is visible, showing proper layering of feathers and the distinct blue speculum patch bordered by white, which is anatomically correct for a drake.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The characteristic upward curl of the central tail feathers (drake feathers) is clearly visible and structurally sound.
